title: Cloud Connector rule endpoints on the wire: which forwarding and DNS rule fields each client sends

prose.text: Traffic forwarding rules (`/ecRules/ecRdr`), DNS rules (`/ecRules/ecDns`) and log and control rules (`/ecRules/self`) share one rule shape, but the contract, the two SDKs and the Terraform provider each model a different subset of it. Paths and field lists are generated; this subject records where the clients disagree with the contract.

{{go-enums-are-comments}} The forwarding method values each source lists, and which token the console's Local method uses, are in [[cloud-connector.forwarding.methods:contract-enums]] and [[cloud-connector.forwarding.methods:local-token]], with the open question of which values the API accepts in [[cloud-connector.forwarding.methods:method-semantics]]. The rule `type` field is separate from the method: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.rule-order:type-ec-rdr]].

Workload group criteria are sent by some clients and absent from the contract {{divergence:workload-groups}}. Whether destination workload groups are accepted, and only on Local rules, is open {{gap:local-switch-acceptance}}; whether `LOCAL_SWITCH` is the Local method's API value is open in [[cloud-connector.terraform.forwarding-rules:local-switch-wire-value]].
The contract and the Go SDK name the ZPA application segment list differently on a write {{divergence:zpa-segments-key}}.

The source IP group exclusion flag is covered in [[cloud-connector.source-ip-groups.rule-use:exclusion-not-in-forwarding-contract]] and [[cloud-connector.source-ip-groups.rule-use:exclusion-terraform-sends]], with the open question in [[cloud-connector.source-ip-groups.rule-use:exclusion-applicability]]. {{ipv6-groups-not-applicable}}

The DNS rule actions differ between the contract (eleven) and Terraform (four): [[cloud-connector.dns.policies:contract-actions]], [[cloud-connector.dns.policies:tf-subset]]; whether one of them is the help's overwrite-DNS-response action is open in [[cloud-connector.dns.policies:response-overwrite]].
{{dns-rule-zpa-ip-group}} The ZTC provider accepts that block but never sends it: [[cloud-connector.terraform.provider-behavior:dns-rule-zpa-ip-group-dropped]].

checks.do: Whether a rule criterion a client sets (workload groups, ZPA segments) is one the contract lists for the write, before trusting that the API applied it.

go-enums-are-comments.statement: In the Go SDK the forwarding rule's `Type` and `ForwardMethod` and the DNS rule's `Action` are plain strings. The supported values of `Type` and `ForwardMethod` appear only in doc comments; the `Action` comment lists no values.

quotes: // The rule action selected from the available options Action string `json:"action,omitempty"`

dns-rule-zpa-ip-group.statement: The contract's DNS rule body has a `zpaIpGroup` reference, which the forwarding rule body does not have; the forwarding rule body takes ZPA application segments instead.

expect.description: An immutable reference to an entity, which consists of ID, name, etc.
The ZPA application segments to which the rule applies.

ipv6-groups-not-applicable.statement: The contract's forwarding rule create body describes both `srcIpv6Groups` and `destIpv6Groups` as not applicable to Cloud & Branch Connector, while the Go SDK's forwarding rule still carries both fields.

expect.description: Not applicable to Cloud & Branch Connector.
Not applicable to Cloud & Branch Connector.

workload-groups.summary: Which sources carry source and destination workload groups on a traffic forwarding rule.

positions.says: The contract's create and update bodies for a forwarding rule have neither `srcWorkloadGroups` nor `destWorkloadGroups`.
The Go SDK's forwarding rule has `srcWorkloadGroups` only.

quotes: // The list of preconfigured workload groups to which the policy must be applied. SrcWorkloadGroups []common.IDNameExtensions `json:"srcWorkloadGroups,omitempty"`

positions.says: The Python SDK maps `src_workload_groups_ids` and `dest_workload_groups_ids` to `srcWorkloadGroups` and `destWorkloadGroups` in the request body, and documents the destination list as valid for the `LOCAL_SWITCH` forward method.
The Python accessor's docstring ties destination workload groups to `LOCAL_SWITCH`.

quotes: dest_workload_groups_ids (list): IDs for destination workload groups (Valid for LOCAL_SWITCH forward method).

positions.says: The ZTC provider sends `src_workload_groups` as the SDK's `SrcWorkloadGroups`; the Go model it uses has no destination field.
The console offers source workload groups on rules of several methods and destination workload groups only for the Local method.

quotes: Destination workload groups can only be applied to Cloud Connector traffic forwarding policies and are only applicable to the Local traffic forwarding method.

workload-groups.impact: The console and the Python SDK show that destination workload groups exist, but the contract documents neither list and the Go SDK and Terraform cannot send a destination list; a destination-workload-group rule can be written only through the Python SDK or a raw call, and no source shows the API's handling of either key.

zpa-segments-key.summary: Under which keys a forwarding rule write carries ZPA application segments and segment groups.

positions.says: The contract's create and update bodies carry `zpaAppSegments` and neither `zpaApplicationSegments` nor `zpaApplicationSegmentGroups`; those two appear only in the rule as read back.

expect.description: The ZPA application segments to which the rule applies.

positions.says: The Go SDK, which the ZTC provider uses, writes the segments as `zpaApplicationSegments`, a field it documents as applicable only to the ECZPA method.
The Go SDK also writes segment groups as `zpaApplicationSegmentGroups`.

The Python SDK documents `zpa_app_segments` for rule writes and maps it to `zpaAppSegments`, the contract's key; it also maps `zpa_application_segments` and `zpa_application_segment_groups` to the read-back keys.
The Python accessor's docstring names `zpa_app_segments` as the rule's ZPA application segments.

quotes: zpa_app_segments (list[dict]): **ZPA Application Segments applicable to the rule.**

zpa-segments-key.impact: A Python caller using the documented `zpa_app_segments` sends the contract's key; a Go or Terraform write sends `zpaApplicationSegments` and `zpaApplicationSegmentGroups`, which the contract lists only in responses. Either the contract's request schema is incomplete or those writes use keys the API does not read on write; no source shows which, so an ECZPA rule written through Go or Terraform should be read back to confirm its segments.

local-switch-acceptance.title: Whether the API accepts destination workload groups on a forwarding rule, and only on Local rules
local-switch-acceptance.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the destination workload groups criterion is a real API field that serializes as `destWorkloadGroups`, valid only on Local (`LOCAL_SWITCH`) rules. The contract lists neither `LOCAL_SWITCH` among the forward methods nor `destWorkloadGroups` among the rule fields; Terraform and the Python SDK send `LOCAL_SWITCH`, and only the Python SDK sends destination workload groups. Whether the API accepts them, and rejects or ignores destination workload groups on rules of other methods, is not shown.
local-switch-acceptance.blocks: building Local forwarding rules with destination workload groups through the API
